absent: Enabled NUMA policy storage, node selection and enforcement logic.
Locking, reference lifetime and completion rules for device page maps beyond guarded release.
Real page migration, compaction and device-private fault flows beyond fallback stubs.
Architectural meaning and enforcement of virtual area flag aliases and arch slots.
Initialization and accounting contexts for total RAM and direct-map bounds.
Failure recovery behaviour for device memory beyond handler presence checks.

findings.text: When NUMA policy support is compiled out, task and VMA policy queries report absence of policy, equality of any two policies holds, and the shared lookup yields no entry while clearing the interleave index. Preference test for many-node preferred mode is available in enabled builds and reports false in disabled builds.

Disabled-build policy lifecycle operations are inert: reference acquire and release do nothing, shared policy setup and teardown do nothing, VMA duplication succeeds without copying, NUMA initialization and default selection do nothing, and task or address-space rebinding accepts a new mask without effect. Huge-node selection clears both outputs and reports node zero, nodemask initialization reports false, page-set migration reports success, string parsing reports failure, and misplacement checks report no preference. Policy and shared-policy types are empty placeholders.

Enabled builds track the highest zone index seen for policy purposes, updating the stored maximum when a larger non-movable zone appears; disabled builds provide an inert variant accepting a plain integer.

Alternate mapping metadata describes a reserved physical window and its consumption: base_pfn marks the start while end_pfn and reserve express fixed bounds, and free combined with align and alloc tracks remaining space and placement.

Device page map descriptor aggregates mapping, lifetime, identity and extent information: an embedded altmap plus reference and completion objects govern lifetime, while a type tag with flags and a vmemmap sizing shift describe kind, and operations with an owner pointer plus a range count and a single-or-flexible range union describe extent.

Device memory owners supply up to four callbacks: release of a folio whose count reached zero with later reuse by core code, migration of unaddressable private memory back to RAM on fault, notification and recovery for failures over a frame interval with fallback to a generic killer when absent or unsupported, and propagation of splits from a head folio to a tail.

Device memory kinds are numbered from one upward with zero reserved for uninitialized values: private and coherent accelerator memory come first, followed by filesystem DAX and generic and PCI peer-to-peer variants.

Folio and page classifiers for private, peer-to-peer, coherent and DAX memory require zone-device status plus a matching type tag, with private and peer-to-peer additionally gated on build configuration. Page forms derive the enclosing folio before applying the folio test, and private-only data accessors validate the private kind before exposing the embedded pointer.

Pagemap utilities expose capability and sizing without side effects: presence of a failure handler, conditional access to the embedded altmap depending on a validity flag, vmemmap multiplicity derived from the stored shift, null lookup and false validity in fallback builds, guarded release of references, page-sized compatibility alignment, and folio initialization that marks large folios remappable when order is nonzero.

Private folio split handling either propagates mapping and pagemap linkage to the new folio when no driver split handler exists or delegates to that handler, with a fully inert variant in fallback builds. Fallback mapping creation warns once and reports an I/O addressing failure, while unmapping does nothing.

Movable page owners provide isolation, migration and return hooks operating on page handles with mode arguments, complemented by folio allocator and releaser function types that carry an opaque private cookie.

Fallback migration primitives report unavailability or inert success: list writeback and target allocation do nothing useful, isolation attempts fail, huge mapping moves and movable-operation registration report unsupported, and misplaced-folio preparation and execution report retryable deferral.

Device migration requests bind a VMA interval to source and destination arrays sized by page count, with cursors for completed and total pages plus start and end bounds, an owner cookie for private memory, flag word and optional fault page. Direction selection uses distinct bits for system and for private, coherent and compound participation.

Migration frame descriptors reserve low bits for state and shift frame numbers above them: validity occupies the lowest bit, migration intent the next, writability and compound state occupy higher low bits, and frame values start at bit six with helpers converting between frames and descriptors.

Migration urgency offers three levels in order: asynchronous, light synchronous, then full synchronous. Early reason codes in order cover compaction, memory failure, hotplug, system call, policy binding and NUMA misplacement.
Later migration reasons in order cover contiguous range moves, long-term pinning, demotion, background reclaim hints, a never-migrated marker and a count sentinel.
Total RAM accounting exposes atomic read plus increment, decrement and add adjustments over a shared counter.

Virtual area flags are defined as individual bit numbers in a bitwise integer type, starting with access and sharing, then protection limits, growth and fault tracking, mapping kinds, locking and I/O hints, copy and accounting controls, huge-page and merge controls, high architecture bits, uncached allowance, droppable and userfault and sealing extensions, with architecture-specific aliases reusing the high and first arch slots and stack direction aliasing growth direction.

Derived virtual area masks shift one by the corresponding bit number, providing read, write, execute, shared, protection-limit and grow-down values plus userfault-missing, with a zero constant denoting no flags.

Page-size utilities convert between pages and megabytes by twenty-minus-shift arithmetic, round addresses up or down to page boundaries, test alignment, and translate between frames, kernel virtual addresses and symbol addresses. Direct-map limits and an all-ones invalid physical address are provided, with one direct-map form using maximum physical bits and the other masking the top bit.
Zeroing of page descriptors supports sizes from 56 through 96 bytes in eight-byte steps, clearing trailing words first then a fixed prefix, with an alternate build using a sized memory set.

Folio utilities compute a member page index by pointer difference, retrieve a folio from the prior link of a list node, report contiguous ranges as always true in this configuration, and report that address spaces never forbid the shared zero page.
Map-count limits reserve five entries for core dumps below the unsigned short maximum, and legacy virtual layout selection is fixed to disabled.
The fallback soft-leaf wait helper warns once and then releases the supplied table lock without waiting.

Debug builds of folio warnings dump the folio and raise a warning when the condition holds, returning the condition value; non-debug builds only validate the condition at compile time. Disabled device-memory mapping and soft-leaf waiting emit a one-time warning to signal unsupported use.
Headers use standard include-once guards to prevent double inclusion.
